content:
Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screen-less fitness band similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who has been using WHOOP for the past six months, I agree that this concept is appealing, but there are several areas where I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in a fairly early stage of development, we don't have many details about the appearance of Apple's screen-less fitness band for now. It's not expected to launch until 2028 at the earliest. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric band with a built-in sensor module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase on a promotional campaign, where Chase Sapphire cardholders could get a WHOOP band at a discount or for free—that's how I got mine. I've been using it since, but I've never fully committed to it.

The reason is simple: automatic exercise detection is never perfect, and having to pull out my phone to log a workout—whether before or after—feels really annoying. With an Apple Watch, you can start tracking a workout directly on the screen, and WHOOP also syncs timing data from Apple Health. That's also the main reason I've kept wearing my Apple Watch.

When I'm at the gym, pulling out my phone is still acceptable, but when I'm cycling or going for a walk, I really don't want the hassle of taking my phone out.

So for Apple's screen-less fitness band, I hope they can add some kind of button and indicator light that lets you start and stop workout tracking. You'd still need to categorise the workout on your phone afterwards, but I'd rather deal with it later than in the moment. Apple could also develop a classification model based on certain factors.

Summary

If Apple can develop a screen-less fitness band that doesn't require a phone and doesn't feel like a hassle, I think it would be very appealing. This kind of design has several advantages, including more comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to be worn alongside a traditional watch.

TB Featured Comments

I bought the FitBit Air because I was fed up with basically only wearing an Apple Watch for the past many years. I love mechanical watches, but at the same time I want to track health data, and I also enjoy the convenience a watch brings, like being able to use Apple Pay without taking out my phone, or unlocking my front door when my hands are full. If Apple launches a similar product that fully integrates into its ecosystem—letting me use a streamlined version of Apple Pay, home key, car key and other NFC functions, plus the ability to connect to AirPods so Siri can read my notifications or perform actions for me—I'll be first in line to buy it.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I found that I still prefer wearing a smartwatch, even if it means sacrificing battery life. I understand some people want a screen-less design to avoid distractions, but for me, I usually just put my watch in Do Not Disturb mode.

What do you think about Apple developing a screen-less fitness band? How much would it need to cost for you to buy one? Let us know in the comments.
